title: Riverbend Privacy and HIM Policy: Denial of Access and Review of a Denial — Medical Records Request (Release of Information)
content:
Policy of Riverbend Regional Health on denying access to records under a Medical Records Request (Release of Information), on the patient's review of a denial, and on the identity and representative-status proof that precede access and release.

## Policy

Access is denied only on a listed ground, in writing, and only for the part of the record the ground covers; the rest is released. On a ground with no review, the denial is final. On a reviewable ground, the patient may ask for review; only the patient (or personal representative) can request it, and a licensed health care professional who took no part in the denial decides within the request type's review decision period, in calendar days, the decision binding Riverbend. A personal representative proves status with one of the documents accepted as proof of personal representative status before any access. Identity is verified before every release.

## Course of a denied request

- When access or release is denied in whole on a listed ground while the request is in process, the request moves from in process to denied.
- When the patient asks for review of a reviewable access denial, the request moves from denied to under review.
- When the reviewing professional reverses the denial, the copy is delivered and the request is fulfilled.
- When the reviewing professional upholds the denial, the request returns to denied.
- When the denial is final, the request is closed.

## Judgement table

| The denial ground | Is review available? | Who may ask for it | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| a ground with no review | no | — | the denial is final |
| a reviewable ground | yes | only the patient or the personal representative | a licensed health care professional who took no part in the denial decides within the review decision period; the decision binds Riverbend |

## Partial denial, on a hypothetical record

A hypothetical request covers a record of which one part falls under a listed ground. The denial, in writing, reaches only that part; the rest of the record is released.

## Points of judgement

- **Grounds**: only a listed ground supports a denial of access.
- **Form**: a denial is in writing.
- **Reach**: a denial covers only the part of the record its ground covers.
- **Who may ask for review**: the patient, or the personal representative, and no one else.
- **Who decides a review**: a licensed health care professional who took no part in the denial.
- **Personal representatives**: status is proved with one of the accepted documents before any access.
- **Identity**: verified before every release.
